mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive two-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing companies and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals an acceleration in economic activity and higher corporate output, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both > 12-month average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month, combined with a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate, signals a rapidly tightening labor market that boosts wage growth and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month +1% AND UNRATE falls in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) for four consecutive months signals weakening residential investment and consumer sentiment, which negatively impacts construction and home-related equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) above their 12-month averages signals broad-based demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and INDPRO both > 12-month average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
